correctness.rationale: A nilpotent partial injection is disjoint chains and has maximal index n precisely for one n-vertex chain. The preserving successor comparison proves the explicit three-branch permutation, identified as first return of modular translation; the precise number of cycles is gcd(b,d), and Farey-neighbor denominators count coprime pairs. For reversal, an orientation-reversing circle homeomorphism swaps two complementary arcs; its square is increasing on each, so the time labels admit only the two opposite even/odd orders, both constructible. The branch intersection is empty for domain size >=3. The standalone checker directly enumerates n! paths for n<=8 and tests the successor structure for m<=30. No finite computation is used as proof of the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: Nilpotency index and the number of elements attaining the maximal depth are canonical semigroup invariants; describing their extremal stratum is a natural question not an arbitrary numerical slice. The theorem distinguishes two natural inverse monoids, identifies all extremal elements via Farey-neighbor arithmetic and a two-type reversal rigidity theorem, and gives their asymptotic growth. It is not claimed to enumerate smaller nilpotency indices or to discover the Sós count.
